email.body1:
Josh, saw Filevine raised $400M, acquired Pincites, and is pushing deeper into enterprise and government with new AI capabilities.

Expanding into those segments usually means more in-market accounts than the business development team can cover before everyone ramps, and that is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Filevine off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Josh, quick follow-up for Filevine.

Post-raise, expectations on pipeline usually climb faster than headcount can, especially pushing into enterprise and government. Most leaders don't know exactly how many meetings the team needs to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Filevine needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Josh, last bit of proof for Filevine.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Filevine's reply rate likely compares to peer legal-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Josh, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling business development without adding headcount isn't a priority right after the raise, no problem at all. The fundraise-to-scale stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise and government motion? I'll tailor it to Filevine either way.
